title: 2.1 Million Cleo AI Users Are Getting FTC Refunds via PayPal
alt_title_1: Why the FTC Is Sending $15.8 Million Back to Cleo AI Users
alt_title_2: Inside the $17 Million FTC Case Against Cash App Cleo AI
description_hook: Starting October 27, 2026, the Federal Trade Commission began sending 2,124,796 PayPal payments totaling more than $15.8 million to users of the cash-advance app Cleo AI, following a $17 million 2025 settlement order in federal court.

affiliate_cta.offer_name: Free 5-Hour Asset Builder OS + reading list
affiliate_cta.pinned_comment: Have you ever paid an express fee on a cash-advance app? Every FTC filing and source for this video is linked in the description.

scenes.headline: 2.1 Million PayPal Refunds Went Out
scenes.narration: Over 2.1 million people are getting PayPal refunds after using an AI cash-advance app. Total payout: more than 15.8 million dollars.

scenes.headline: Promised Up to $250 Today
scenes.narration: The FTC says Cleo's ads promised up to 250 or 500 dollars today, if users paid for a monthly subscription.
scenes.source: FTC v. Cleo AI, No. 1:25-cv-02594, Complaint p. 5 (S.D.N.Y.)

scenes.headline: Almost Nobody Got $250
scenes.narration: The FTC alleged only 0.3 percent of Plus borrowers got the full 250 dollars, and paid express transfers could still arrive the next day.
scenes.source: FTC v. Cleo AI, Complaint (S.D.N.Y. filed Mar/May 2025)

scenes.headline: Blocked From Canceling
scenes.narration: It also alleged users with an unpaid advance could not cancel. Cleo settled for 17 million dollars, and no court ruled on the claims.

scenes.headline: Count Fees Like Interest
scenes.right_body: Monthly fee + express fee on tiny sums
scenes.narration: When a small advance requires a subscription plus a rush fee, treat both fees as interest before you tap accept.
